Community Health Nursing Approaches & Home Visits

Community nursing approaches — home visits, surveys, school and industry health, and working with volunteers.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the purpose and process of a home visit
  • Explain community surveys and records
  • Describe school and industrial health programmes
  • Involve community volunteers in care

In simple words

The community health nurse reaches people where they live and work. The home visit is the basic tool; the survey finds out who needs what, and volunteers keep the care going.

Home visit

Purpose: assess the home and family, provide care, teach, find new problems and establish trust.

Process:

  1. Planning — set priority (newborn, high risk, referral follow-up), time and route
  2. Before entry — comb hair, wear clean uniform and shoes, greet the family
  3. Introduction — introduce yourself and state the purpose in simple words
  4. Observation — people, house, water source, food, sanitation, environment
  5. Nursing care — examination, teaching, demonstration and recording
  6. Summary — agree on what the family will do and when you will return
  7. Closure — thank the family, sign the visit, and record

Other community approaches

Approach What the nurse does
Community survey Lists families, maps needs, sets priorities
Health camps Mass screening, immunisation and referral
School health Immunisation, anaemia and eye checks, hygiene classes
Industrial health Occupational hazard checks, first aid, health education
Home-based care Bed-ridden, elderly and palliative patients

Working with volunteers

  • ASHA — first contact, mobilises families, gives essential medicines
  • Anganwadi worker — nutrition, preschool and growth monitoring
  • Mahila groups and self-help groups — support, loans, health education
  • Village health committee — local decisions and resources
  • Nurses train, supervise and never replace these workers

🔴 Do not break the trust of the home

Keep every promise, speak in the family’s language, keep what you learn confidential and never compare families unfavourably. Trust is the tool that makes future visits work.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Home visit steps: plan, enter, observe, care, teach, close and record.
  2. Set the priority of the visit from the family folder.
  3. ASHA is the first contact person in the village.
  4. The nurse trains and supervises volunteers but does not replace them.
  5. Home visits build trust for all future community work.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Watch water source, drainage, ventilation and food storage during the visit.
  2. School health includes immunisation, anaemia checks and oral health.
  3. Industrial health screens occupational hazards and gives first aid.
  4. Health camps are screening events, not substitute for routine services.
  5. Record every visit in the family folder for continuity.

📌 Memory trick

Visit = PEOCT: Plan, Enter and greet, Observe, Care and teach, Thank and record.

60-second revision

  • Home visit: plan, enter, observe, assess, teach, close, record.
  • Priority: newborns, high-risk mothers, referral follow-up.
  • Other approaches: survey, camps, school and industrial health.
  • Volunteers: ASHA, Anganwadi, self-help groups, village committee.
  • Trust and confidentiality are essential.

Test yourself

The first step of a home visit is:

Answer: B. Planning the priority, time and route, and preparing the kit come first.

Who is the first contact person in the village under the ASHA scheme?

Answer: B. ASHA is a community woman trained to link the community to the health system.

Which is checked during the observation part of the visit?

Answer: B. Observation covers people, water source, drainage, ventilation, food storage and sanitation.

Health camps are mainly used for:

Answer: A. Camps screen many people quickly and refer those who need further care.

The nurse’s role with village volunteers is to:

Answer: B. The nurse trains, guides and supervises volunteers so that care continues between visits.
